title: Parallel developer spawns share one git index, so explicit-path staging is not safe
description:
Observed live on 2026-08-02, twice, during the parallel TASK-183 / TASK-184 drive. Filed against the ORCHESTRATION protocol, not against either ticket's code — both developers behaved correctly and one of them caught and repaired the problem itself.

**What happened.** Two `developer` subagents were spawned concurrently against deliberately disjoint file surfaces (packs/reconciler vs docs/sensor), each briefed to stage only its own files with `git add <explicit paths>` and never `git add -A`. Both followed that instruction. It was not sufficient.

TASK-184's developer ran `git add` with exactly its 3 files, then `git commit` — and the resulting commit `a64859c` contained **11 files**, having swept up TASK-183's concurrently-uncommitted work (`bin/pack-ctl.js`, `dist/pack-ctl.cjs`, `src/pack-apply.js`, `src/plugin-root.js` and four spec files). The sibling agent had staged its own work in the window between the first agent's `add` and its `commit`. It was caught via `git show --stat HEAD` immediately after committing, repaired with `git reset --soft HEAD~1` followed by `git reset HEAD -- <the 8 foreign files>`, and recommitted cleanly as the docs-only `ff1d07b`. TASK-183's developer independently confirmed its files returned to the working tree byte-identical and later committed them as `0a76ae2`.

Outcome this time: no content lost, history linear, nothing pushed, both tickets landed correctly. But the recovery depended on one agent voluntarily verifying its own commit after the fact.

**Root cause.** `git add <paths>` followed by `git commit` is **not atomic** with respect to a sibling process operating on the same index. Disjoint FILE surfaces do not give disjoint INDEX access — the index is the shared resource, and the briefing constraint addressed the wrong one. A `git commit -- <paths>` (pathspec-limited commit, which bypasses the index) or per-agent worktree isolation would not have had this failure.

**Why this matters beyond a one-off.** The framework actively encourages this shape: the orchestrator-routing skill's delegation protocol says to "spawn subagents in parallel whenever their work is independent", and nothing in `agents/developer.md` or the routing skill warns that independence of files is not independence of the index. The next parallel drive will hit the same hazard, and it may not be caught — a silently over-broad commit attributes one ticket's changes to another ticket's commit message, corrupting the audit trail that `linked_commits` and the review process both depend on.

**Fix direction (decide, do not assume).** At least three options, and they are not equivalent:
1. **Worktree isolation** — the `Agent` tool supports `isolation: 'worktree'`, giving each agent its own checkout. Strongest fix, removes the shared index entirely. Costs setup time and disk per agent, and needs a merge/handback story for the commits produced there.
2. **Pathspec-limited commit** — instruct developers to use `git commit -- <explicit paths>`, which commits the named paths directly and does not depend on prior `git add`. Cheap, but still relies on the agent following instructions correctly.
3. **Serialize the commit step** — keep parallel implementation but funnel commits through a lock (the repo already has an advisory session lock in `src/session-lock.js` that could be reused). Middle cost.

Whichever is chosen, the mandatory post-commit verification (`git show --stat HEAD` immediately after committing, confirming the file list matches what was intended) should become part of the developer briefing regardless — it is what saved this incident, and it is nearly free.
acceptance_criteria: The hazard is reproduced deterministically in a test: two concurrent stage-then-commit sequences against disjoint paths in one repo, demonstrating that a commit can capture the sibling's staged files. If a deterministic reproduction proves impractical (it is a race), state why and instead lock the CHOSEN mitigation's behavior directly — do not ship an untested claim that the problem is fixed.

A mitigation is chosen from the three options in the description (worktree isolation, pathspec-limited commit, or serialized commits) and the reasoning is recorded in the closing comment, including what it costs and what it does NOT protect against.

The chosen mitigation is implemented where the orchestrator actually spawns developers — i.e. the guidance lives in agents/developer.md and/or the orchestrator-routing delegation protocol, in BOTH parity copies byte-identically, not only in a ticket comment.

The orchestrator-routing skill's 'spawn subagents in parallel whenever their work is independent' guidance is amended to state explicitly that disjoint FILE surfaces do not imply safe concurrent commits, so the next parallel drive is not briefed the same wrong way this one was.

Mandatory post-commit verification (git show --stat HEAD immediately after committing, asserting the file list matches intent) is added to the developer briefing contract regardless of which mitigation is chosen — it is what caught this incident and it is nearly free.
npm run test:all is green; no existing spec regresses; if any bundled source changed, dist rebuilt and committed with dist-parity passing.
